# mid-E co-scheduling: probe_gemm A (sequential bucket launches, shipped shape) vs B (co-resident slabs,
# one launch). Qwen3.8@2.05 layer 12, WARM_S=3, ks=2. B/A < 1 means co-scheduling wins.
# Why: live routing puts ~124 eligible experts in ONE launch at R=2048, between the measured rungs
# E=16 (B loses) and E=512 (B wins 9-16%). D17 could not decide its own operating point without this.
# generated by run_plan_close2.sh S3

=== READOUT ==============================================================
B/A (one-launch co-resident slabs vs sequential bucket launches), Qwen3.8@2.05 layer 12, ks=2:
   E=128 rows=64   A 928.3 us   B 875.5 us   ->  B/A 0.943   (co-scheduling wins 6.0 pct)
   E=256 rows=64   A 1826.9 us  B 1741.1 us  ->  B/A 0.953   (wins 4.9 pct)
   E=128 rows=32   A 468.2 us   B 439.2 us   ->  B/A 0.938   (wins 6.6 pct)
D17 MISSING RUNG, FILLED. Live routing at R=2048 puts ~124 eligible experts in one launch, which sat between
the only two measured points (E=16: B loses, 0.97-1.15; E=512: B wins 9-16 pct). It now has a rung at the
operating point: co-scheduling is worth 5-6 pct there, i.e. real but smaller than at E=512. Gain is
monotone-ish in E (16: <1 no, 128: 0.94, 256: 0.95, 512: 0.85-0.91) and flat in rows (32 and 64 agree).
The bracketing constant in slab_advice (2*E*bytes > 10x L2) can now be relaxed to about 4x L2: E=128 with
0.38 MiB per projection is 96 MiB = 4.0x L2 and B already wins. Replace the constant with these rungs at
the next planner touch (do not leave a made-up threshold in code once a measurement exists).
Variant A also confirms the per-bucket primitive (D18): 928.3/128 = 7.25 and 1826.9/256 = 7.14 us per
expert-projection bucket at K=2 rows=64 -- linear in experts to 1.5 pct, so cost is per bucket.
